newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end mixed, still nervous.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end mixed, still nervous.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished mixed Friday with the local market rising and Brady bonds continuing their tumble from earlier in the week.
Traders said the market was still very jittery after the shake out Wednesday and Thursday following statements by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's.
"I am recommending investors to be very cautious in the short term over U.S. indicators," said Roberta Costa Bourdieu, senior fixed income analyst at Banco Rio.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.53 to 126.35 and Argentina's FRB due 2005 fell 1/4 to 90-1/4.
"The fact is that the market is very nervous, so I would suggest not going long even if prices are attractive now," added Bourdieu.
Traders said the market is set to pay more attention to U.S. indicators now that Greenspan has pointed to the possibility of a hike in rates to control inflation.
Next week's release of the U.S. February unemployment report, expected Friday, will be watched very closely as players search for the inflation signs that may be spooking Greenspan.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 5.38 percent from 5.53 percent.
